title: Reconcile similarity scoring behavior for legacy clients and normalized storage
creator: Ava Carter
description:
Summary: Several customers and internal tests found inconsistent similarity scores coming from the embeddings + reranker pipeline after recent optimizations. Root causes include: (1) implicit normalization applied at different layers (SDK, DB pre-processing, runtime), (2) stored vectors sometimes saved in post-quantization space without a stored norm, and (3) legacy clients relying on raw dot-product semantics. This ticket implements a compatibility-first fix: make scoring semantics explicit, add a runtime shim for legacy clients, and migrate stored vectors to a clear canonical representation while keeping a safe rollback path.

Goals: 
- Make similarity mode deterministic and explicit (accept "cosine","dot_raw","dot_normalized").
- Ensure on-disk/vector-store representation is self-describing (store norm field when possible).
- Provide a server-side compatibility shim that preserves existing scores for clients that opt into legacy behavior.
- Optimize fast-path for pre-normalized vectors to avoid extra compute on hot paths and preserve current latency SLOs (p99 < 40ms for single-rerank requests).

Non-goals: automatic rewriting of arbitrary third-party vector stores (we provide tooling, not force-conversion).
comments: 2026-03-02 - Triage: Ava ran failure repro locally. Reproduced mismatch between SDK v2 which normalized client-side and runtime v1.18 which expected raw vectors. Assigned to Liam.

2026-03-03 - Design decision: agreed on explicit query param similarity_mode and a compatibility header X-RW-Embed-Compat with values {legacy-v1, normalized-v2}. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Embedding+Scoring+Compat

2026-03-04 - Trade-off: decided not to change default runtime scoring to cosine immediately because it would break >50 internal integration tests. We'll expose new default in SDK 1 major release and keep runtime default unchanged behind compat header.
2026-03-05 - Implementation note: added 'norm' to on-disk schema for vectorstore rows (nullable for older rows). Runtime will compute norm on-read for rows without norm and backfill asynchronously.

2026-03-06 - Benchmark: microbench with 4k-dim vectors shows computing norm on the hot path adds ~1.8ms median; ensuring pre-normalized fast-path avoids that cost. Target p50 < 15ms, p99 < 40ms maintained in canary.

2026-03-07 - Code review (PR feedback): @sanjay requested explicit handling for zero-length vectors and quantized int8 pathological cases; added guard to return similarity 0 and log anomaly. PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/3124

2026-03-08 - QA: ran evals on 3 internal rerank prompt sets. Cosine vs dot_normalized agreement improves MRR on two sets by +1.2% and +0.8% respectively. Noted one customer-specific corpus where legacy dot_raw had slightly better ordering; will expose as per-client override.

2026-03-09 - Ops: canary rollout plan drafted. Phase 1: 5% traffic with X-RW-Embed-Compat=legacy-v1 to match existing behavior. Phase 2: 20% with migration backfill enabled. Metrics dashboard: embeddings/score-delta, rerank-MRR, latency-by-sim-mode.
2026-03-10 - Next: finish backfill worker, add SDK default change PR, and prepare customer communications for breaking-change window if we flip default later)
